title: Is it safe to drink Red Bull and vodka? Dubious research tied to the company has shaped energy drink policy.
byline: Sasha Chavkin, Ashley Okwuosa, Fernanda Aguirre, Romina Colman
excerpt: The company paid scientists whose studies largely found that mixing energy drinks and alcohol isn’t harmful, contrary to most research.
content_html:
This story, co-published by STAT, is part of the Behind the Buzz project, an investigative collaboration involving The Examination, The Bristol Cable, Daraj, Investico, Paper Trail Media, Der Spiegel, Der Standard and the Toronto Star.

On a winter morning in a Long Island town about two hours east of New York City’s skyscrapers, a Dutch researcher told local officials that their concerns about mixing heavily caffeinated energy drinks with alcohol were overblown.

A few months earlier, the U.S. Food and Drug Administration had effectively banned Four Loko, a caffeinated malt liquor dubbed “blackout in a can” by college students. Suburban Suffolk County was now considering something more sweeping: a ban on selling energy drinks to minors.

Joris Verster, an academic from Utrecht University, said there was no scientific basis for the law. Though booze and energy drinks are often consumed together, Verster argued that beverages like Red Bull aren’t to blame for bad things that happen when people get drunk. 

He offered an analogy that might resonate with locals; Suffolk County includes the beach towns that inspired the thriller “Jaws.” Blaming energy drinks for binge drinking and alcohol-fueled injuries, he said, would be like blaming shark attacks on summertime ice cream sales.

“The shark attacks are not caused by the ice cream sales,” Verster said in the February 2011 hearing. 

He was one of three scientists who had crossed the Atlantic to urge officials to drop the proposal. The others were a British professor and Red Bull’s chief scientific officer. The trio shared more than a research interest: Through paychecks or research grants, all three had gotten money from Red Bull, the world’s largest energy drink company.

Their argument won the day. Lawmakers dropped the age limit, marking an early victory for the Austria-based company in what would become a global campaign to use science to combat restrictions on its products.

For more than a decade, Red Bull paid hundreds of thousands of dollars for university professors to conduct research that has been favorable to the energy drink industry, a joint investigation involving The Examination, The Bristol Cable, Daraj, Investico, Paper Trail Media, Der Spiegel, Der Standard, STAT and the Toronto Star found. The company has flown academics to U.S. cities and provided talking points for meetings with government officials who were considering restrictions on energy drinks. It funded a doctorate for a researcher in the United Kingdom and another in the Netherlands. 

In the United States and Canada, research backed by Red Bull or conducted by academics with financial ties to the company has been used to defeat measures such as age restrictions and warning labels. 

A pivotal report by a European food agency in 2015 cited these studies in finding that there wasn’t clear evidence that mixing energy drinks and alcohol was harmful. That report remains the last word in Europe and has been used to prevent action elsewhere.

The studies backed by Red Bull have been nearly unanimous in their message: Consuming energy drinks and alcohol together is no more harmful than drinking alcohol alone. 

That stands in stark contrast to the vast majority of independent studies on the subject.

The Examination gathered more than 100 studies about the health or behavioral risks of mixing energy drinks and alcohol. Of the studies that received funding by Red Bull or were conducted by researchers who disclosed financial conflicts of interest with the company, 95% concluded that mixing alcohol with energy drinks did not increase those risks. Roughly 80% of independent studies reached the opposite conclusion, The Examination found.

Companies often fund research into controversial products, a practice that is criticized by health advocates. But leading alcohol researchers who reviewed some of the studies with financial ties to Red Bull said there are deeper problems.

A number of the studies are flawed, they said, raising questions about their conclusions. In Boston, a team of scientists withdrew from a Red Bull-funded study after Verster, the Dutch researcher, refused to address problems they believed would bias the results.

In a brief statement to The Examination and its partners, Karlheinz Niederreiter, Global Head of Science, Regulatory and Government Affairs at Red Bull, wrote, “Health authorities across the world have concluded that Red Bull Energy Drink is safe to consume.” That’s why, he wrote, nearly 14 billion cans were sold worldwide last year. 

Niederreiter and other Red Bull executives did not answer questions about the news outlets’ findings, including those about the safety of consuming energy drinks with alcohol.

Voluntary guidelines published by American and European industry groups say their member companies, which include Red Bull and Monster Beverage Corp., don’t promote mixing energy drinks with alcohol and don’t claim that energy drinks counteract the effects of alcohol. The European group said academic research has found that mixing the two doesn’t pose additional risks.

Peter Miller, a professor at Deakin University in Australia, said the news outlets’ findings weren’t surprising. Back in 2013, around the time that much of this research was published, he wrote an essay in a medical journal criticizing the wave of industry-funded studies about mixing energy drinks and alcohol. 

Those research grants are “an investment using universities’ reputation to be able to influence policy,” Miller told The Examination. “This is a campaign to protect their profits and to avoid legislative intervention.”

And it’s worked, he said. Red Bull-funded researchers have “absolutely undermined the evidence base,” Miller said. “It leads to this doubt where politicians don't act.”

Much of this research was conducted at a time of growing public debate about the safety of energy drinks. Especially for young people. And especially in combination with alcohol.

Wide-awake drunk

One weekend night in August 2016, Zachary Mitchell joined some friends for a getaway at a lakeside cottage in Quebec. The 21-year-old visited the cottage nearly every summer weekend, his mother said.

Mitchell drank several cans of Red Bull and about six beers over about two hours before he and his friends decided to go for a swim, according to a coroner's report.

Mitchell had been born near a lake and learned to swim from a young age. “He was a fish,” said his mother, Heather Mitchell.

But shortly before midnight, Mitchell hit the water awkwardly when he dove from a 15-foot high deck. He briefly resurfaced, spoke a few words and went under again. That was the last his friends saw of him, according to a coroner's report.

The coroner wrote that Mitchell had drowned, likely due to an arrhythmia triggered by the combination of energy drinks and physical exercise. She noted that he had a blood-alcohol content of about 0.1%, slightly over the legal limit for driving. 

In her report, she called for a “vast advertising awareness campaign targeting a young audience” about the risks of energy drinks, including those from combining them with alcohol.

Researchers have a term that captures their concern about mixing alcohol and energy drinks: wide-awake drunk.

Tim Stockwell, who headed the Canadian Institute for Substance Use Research from 2004 to 2020, said adding the stimulation of energy drinks to the impaired judgment caused by alcohol is a recipe for risky behavior. 

The caffeine in energy drinks ranges from 80 mg in a Red Bull, slightly less than a typical cup of coffee, to 300 mg in other brands. But energy drinks also contain ingredients such as taurine and guarana that can magnify its effects on the body.

“It's a pretty potentially dangerous combination, giving you the energy to do crazy, daft things,” Stockwell said, “and something that takes away the fear of the consequences.”

People have been hurt or killed all over the world after consuming alcohol and energy drinks, according to news reports. In England, an 18-year-old woman suffered three cardiac arrests after downing 10 Jägerbombs, a cocktail that combines an energy drink with the spirit Jägermeister. In Washington state, a 17-year-old boy died of acute alcohol intoxication after mixing hard liquor and energy drinks while playing video games with friends. In Quebec, a 14-year-old girl was found dead behind her school after consuming a caffeinated alcoholic drink called FCKD UP.

A considerable body of research suggests that incidents like these aren’t just chance or circumstance. Mixing alcohol and energy drinks was linked to higher rates of binge drinking, sexual abuse and drunk driving, according to a study conducted among U.S. college students. Another study of hospital patients in Canada found the combination was tied to higher levels of injury; among women, the risk of injury tripled.

Health authorities have shared these views. The U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention warn that mixing alcohol and energy drinks can lead to more drinking and a greater risk of injury, drunk driving and unwanted or unprotected sex.

This research was just emerging back in 2010 during a string of deaths involving young people and Four Loko. The FDA acted quickly, ordering Four Loko and other companies to stop selling caffeinated alcoholic drinks.

At the time of Mitchell’s death, energy drinks in Canada carried a warning saying not to mix them with alcohol. The coroner investigating his death criticized those warnings, writing that they were “insufficient” and “in small print.”

Heather Mitchell said that neither she nor her son were fully aware of the risks of energy drinks. She said she really didn’t know if he frequently drank them. She assumed that if they were on the shelf, they were safe.

Red Bull gets into the research business

In 2011, soon after becoming director of an injury prevention research center at Boston University, Jonathan Howland joined two Red Bull executives for dinner. One of them was Niederreiter, who was in charge of science for the company. Lobster was on the menu and a scientific collaboration was taking shape.

Howland, who believed the FDA had overstepped the evidence with its ban on caffeinated alcoholic beverages, had taken note of ongoing research by Verster, the Dutch professor. The two ran in similar academic circles; both were members of a small group of researchers who studied alcohol hangovers. Verster’s preliminary findings suggested that mixing alcohol and energy drinks did not cause people to drink more or suffer higher rates of harm.

When Verster said he wanted to replicate his study in the United States, Howland didn’t hesitate. “I just jumped on it,” he said in an interview. That led to a deal between Red Bull and Boston University.

The key to Verster’s research was that he didn’t look for differences between people who drank only alcohol and people who consumed both alcohol and energy drinks, Verster told The Examination. Instead, he built his studies around people who did both, comparing outcomes between when they consumed alcohol alone and when they consumed it with energy drinks.

This eliminated variables such as personality type and enabled him to test for causality, Verster said.

But several months after Howland and his team started the project, they discovered a problem in how the study was set up. The details of the dispute were laid out in emails, study documents, and interviews with Howland and Tamara Calise, who consulted with the Boston team as a research expert.

The Boston researchers were alarmed because the survey that Verster’s team had provided defined alcohol mixed with energy drinks to include only alcoholic beverages consumed within two hours of an energy drink. That could underestimate binge drinking and harm linked to energy drinks, Howland’s team determined. There was no restriction on which drinks were counted when participants drank alcohol alone.

Howland and his colleagues urged Verster to change his approach. Verster refused. Howland said the message was clear: that “if you want the money, you do it exactly the way we tell you.”

Howland's team ultimately decided to back out of the study.

“We decided that we cannot use our university positions and professional reputations to recruit for a study that we believe cannot test important hypotheses in an unbiased way,” Howland wrote to Verster in June 2012.

That didn’t seem to affect Red Bull’s support of Verster’s research. Later that year, he and four colleagues published a study of Dutch students, funded by the company, that used the disputed approach and came to a surprising conclusion: People were better off when they mixed alcohol with energy drinks than when they drank alcohol alone. When they combined the two, they drank less alcohol and were less likely to suffer harmful consequences, the study concluded.

Five alcohol researchers consulted by The Examination said they agreed with the Boston researchers that the approach by Verster’s team was flawed. The half-life of caffeine is five to six hours — meaning that five to six hours after someone ingests caffeine, half of it remains in their system and continues to affect them. That’s significantly longer than the time window used by Verster.

From 2016 to 2021, Verster and other Red Bull-funded scientists in the U.K. and Australia published at least five more studies that used the same definition of mixing alcohol and energy drinks. All concluded that mixing did not lead to increased drinking or harm. 

Laura Schmidt, a professor at the University of California, San Francisco who has examined research funded by the food and beverage industry, described those studies as “marketing dressed up as science.” 

William Kerr, scientific director at the federally funded National Alcohol Research Center, said, “Aspects of the studies seem biased to deliver counterintuitive results that support industry perspectives.” 

We decided that we cannot use our university positions and professional reputations to recruit for a study that we believe cannot test important hypotheses in an unbiased way.

Jonathan Howland, in an email to Joris Verster in June 2012

In an email to The Examination, Verster acknowledged that the Boston researchers raised questions about the study methodology. He said he didn’t change it because he wanted the study to be comparable to his earlier research.

Regarding his definition of mixing of alcoholic and energy drinks, he wrote that the two-hour limit was meant to exclude energy drinks consumed much earlier in the day, not to limit the number of alcoholic drinks counted.

Utrecht University investigated potential conflicts of interest in Verster’s partnership with Red Bull more than a decade ago. The university determined that Verster was insufficiently transparent because he had been paid through his own company for studies that cited his university affiliation. However, the university concluded this wasn’t a breach of integrity. 

After recent inquiries by the Dutch news outlet Investico about Verster’s studies, the university said that Verster had run afoul of its policy governing outside-funded research. The university said it didn’t know the extent of that work and that it was a problem for Verster to continue to be paid privately while citing his university affiliation.

The university said the inquiries had “prompted internal questions” and that it was setting up a committee to investigate the “scientific culture and scientific quality policy” within Verster’s research group.

Verster, the most prolific among the Red Bull-backed researchers, denied that he violated ethical guidelines and said he stands by his research. He chalked up criticisms of his work to scientific disagreements.

Sean Johnson, whose doctorate was funded by Red Bull and who published several studies with Verster, has expressed reservations about how the Red Bull-funded research was conducted, the U.K.’s Bristol Cable has found.

Johnson reflected on his early research in a commentary submitted in 2023 as part of his doctoral submission. He wrote that research on mixing alcohol and energy drinks seemed to have become politicized; at times, going through the peer review process “felt like you were in the trenches.” Later, his perspective on that period shifted.

“I may have developed an unconscious bias towards my academic group and industry funders position,” Johnson wrote. In parentheses after “funders,” he wrote, “Red Bull GmbH.”

Johnson did not respond to repeated requests for comment.

‘Science is science, regardless of who is funding it’

The number of studies with financial ties to Red Bull about the risks of alcohol and energy drinks is relatively small, but that body of research has been influential nonetheless. Reports on energy drink policy by government or advisory bodies in the United Kingdom, Canada, Australia, Spain and Ireland have cited these studies, The Examination found.

The most significant was a report by the European Food Safety Authority. As the European Union’s scientific adviser on food issues, its opinions not only inform policy in Europe, but also carry weight internationally. 

In 2015, that agency released a sweeping report that broadly endorsed the safety of caffeine and energy drinks. Three sections addressing the combination of energy drinks and alcohol cited Verster’s studies. 

The most detailed discussion was drawn from a 2014 study authored by Verster and three colleagues who had previously received Red Bull funding. They reviewed laboratory studies to determine whether mixing alcohol and caffeine caused people to get drunk without realizing it, a phenomenon known as “masking.” They concluded that masking was not a threat.

Though masking was a subject of research at the time, several alcohol researchers told The Examination, it’s not the most serious issue when it comes to energy drinks and alcohol. Far more significant, they said, is that energy drinks can prime people to drink more alcohol and that the combination of the two creates a sense of excitement and disinhibition — “wide-awake drunk.”

The European food authority’s report echoed Verster and his colleagues’ conclusion that masking — and more generally, mixing alcohol and energy drinks — was not a serious concern. The food authority’s report didn’t note that the studies disclosed researchers’ ties to Red Bull. 

Silvia Valtueña Martínez, a European Food Safety Authority scientist who contributed to its 2015 report, defended its findings. The authors considered a wide range of research, she said, and industry-backed studies like Red Bull’s should not be discounted. 

“Science is science, regardless of who is funding it,” she said.

Although the food authority recently said it would revisit its findings on caffeine and energy drinks, Malta Today reported that it doesn’t plan to address the risks of mixing energy drinks and alcohol.

For more than a decade, the food authority’s report has been a key reference regarding energy drinks in Europe and beyond; government and advisory bodies in the United Kingdom, Canada, Germany and other countries have cited it.

So too has the beverage industry, using it to argue against regulations on energy drinks. 

Science is science, regardless of who is funding it.

Silvia Valtueña Martínez, European Food Safety Authority scientist

One of those efforts was in Canada, several years after Mitchell’s death.

The alcohol warning label that was on energy drink cans when he died was the result of a temporary measure. In 2021, Health Canada, the country’s public health agency, proposed making the warning permanent, noting that mixing alcohol with energy drinks had been “identified as a public health concern.” 

The beverage industry said there was no scientific basis for the warning label — and it had research to back up its position.

The Canadian Beverage Association sent Health Canada a letter citing three studies. All of them had authors who had received funding from Red Bull. The European Union joined in, cautioning against the labeling requirement and pointing to the European Food Safety Authority report.

A year later, Health Canada did an about-face, not only abandoning its proposal to make the warning label permanent, but dropping it altogether. 

In a written statement, Health Canada told The Examination and the Toronto Star that it “relied heavily” on the 2015 European food authority report, as well as its own risk assessments, in making the decision. The agency said it considered “a broad range of information,” including published studies and stakeholder submissions. 

Heather Mitchell called Health Canada’s decision “a clear dereliction of duty.” 

Nearly a decade after she lost her son, energy drink cans in Canada provide less information about alcohol risks than they did on the night he died. 

Aisvarya Chandrasekar, a computational journalist at the Tow Center for Digital Journalism at Columbia University, contributed to the data analysis. 

Léopold Salzenstein, a data reporter at The Examination, and Rachel Auslander, a freelance journalist, contributed reporting.

In parentheses after “funders,” he wrote, “Red Bull GmbH.”Johnson did not respond to repeated requests for comment.‘Science is science, regardless of who is funding it’The European Food Safety Authority cited research by scientists with financial ties to Red Bull in deciding that mixing alcohol and energy drinks wasn’t a serious health concern. The food authority’s report was later cited by Health Canada in deciding to drop a requirement that energy drink cans warn people against consuming them with alcohol.Illustration by The Examination/Evident MediaThe number of studies with financial ties to Red Bull about the risks of alcohol and energy drinks is relatively small, but that body of research has been influential nonetheless. Reports on energy drink policy by government or advisory bodies in the United Kingdom, Canada, Australia, Spain and Ireland have cited these studies, The Examination found.The most significant was a report by the European Food Safety Authority. As the European Union’s scientific adviser on food issues, its opinions not only inform policy in Europe, but also carry weight internationally. In 2015, that agency released a sweeping report that broadly endorsed the safety of caffeine and energy drinks. Three sections addressing the combination of energy drinks and alcohol cited Verster’s studies. The most detailed discussion was drawn from a 2014 study authored by Verster and three colleagues who had previously received Red Bull funding. They reviewed laboratory studies to determine whether mixing alcohol and caffeine caused people to get drunk without realizing it, a phenomenon known as “masking.” They concluded that masking was not a threat.Though masking was a subject of research at the time, several alcohol researchers told The Examination, it’s not the most serious issue when it comes to energy drinks and alcohol. Far more significant, they said, is that energy drinks can prime people to drink more alcohol and that the combination of the two creates a sense of excitement and disinhibition — “wide-awake drunk.”The European food authority’s report echoed Verster and his colleagues’ conclusion that masking — and more generally, mixing alcohol and energy drinks — was not a serious concern. The food authority’s report didn’t note that the studies disclosed researchers’ ties to Red Bull. Silvia Valtueña Martínez, a European Food Safety Authority scientist who contributed to its 2015 report, defended its findings. The authors considered a wide range of research, she said, and industry-backed studies like Red Bull’s should not be discounted. “Science is science, regardless of who is funding it,” she said.Although the food authority recently said it would revisit its findings on caffeine and energy drinks, Malta Today reported that it doesn’t plan to address the risks of mixing energy drinks and alcohol.For more than a decade, the food authority’s report has been a key reference regarding energy drinks in Europe and beyond; government and advisory bodies in the United Kingdom, Canada, Germany and other countries have cited it.So too has the beverage industry, using it to argue against regulations on energy drinks. Science is science, regardless of who is funding it.Silvia Valtueña Martínez, European Food Safety Authority scientist One of those efforts was in Canada, several years after Mitchell’s death.The alcohol warning label that was on energy drink cans when he died was the result of a temporary measure. In 2021, Health Canada, the country’s public health agency, proposed making the warning permanent, noting that mixing alcohol with energy drinks had been “identified as a public health concern.” The beverage industry said there was no scientific basis for the warning label — and it had research to back up its position.The Canadian Beverage Association sent Health Canada a letter citing three studies. All of them had authors who had received funding from Red Bull. The European Union joined in, cautioning against the labeling requirement and pointing to the European Food Safety Authority report.A year later, Health Canada did an about-face, not only abandoning its proposal to make the warning label permanent, but dropping it altogether. In a written statement, Health Canada told The Examination and the Toronto Star that it “relied heavily” on the 2015 European food authority report, as well as its own risk assessments, in making the decision. The agency said it considered “a broad range of information,” including published studies and stakeholder submissions. Heather Mitchell called Health Canada’s decision “a clear dereliction of duty.” Nearly a decade after she lost her son, energy drink cans in Canada provide less information about alcohol risks than they did on the night he died. Aisvarya Chandrasekar, a computational journalist at the Tow Center for Digital Journalism at Columbia University, contributed to the data analysis. sentences.zh: 她指出，他的血液酒精含量约为 0.1%，略高于驾驶的法定上限。

blocks.html_en: In her report, she called for a “vast advertising awareness campaign targeting a young audience” about the risks of energy drinks, including those from combining them with alcohol.

sentences.en: In her report, she called for a “vast advertising awareness campaign targeting a young audience” about the risks of energy drinks, including those from combining them with alcohol.
sentences.zh: 她在报告中呼吁“针对年轻受众开展大规模的广告宣传活动”，宣传能量饮料的风险，包括将其与酒精混合的风险。

sentences.en: Mitchell, pictured diving into Lake Saint Pierre in Quebec on another occasion, grew up around the water and was a strong swimmer, his mother, Heather Mitchell, recalled.
sentences.zh: 米切尔的母亲希瑟·米切尔回忆说，米切尔在另一次照片中跳入魁北克的圣皮埃尔湖，他是在水边长大的，是一位游泳健将。

sentences.en: “He was a fish,” she said.Photos provided by Heather Mitchell
sentences.zh: “他是一条鱼，”她说。照片由希瑟·米切尔提供

blocks.html_en: Researchers have a term that captures their concern about mixing alcohol and energy drinks: wide-awake drunk.

sentences.en: Researchers have a term that captures their concern about mixing alcohol and energy drinks: wide-awake drunk.
sentences.zh: 研究人员有一个术语来表达他们对混合酒精和能量饮料的担忧：完全清醒的醉酒。

blocks.html_en: Tim Stockwell, who headed the Canadian Institute for Substance Use Research from 2004 to 2020, said adding the stimulation of energy drinks to the impaired judgment caused by alcohol is a recipe for risky behavior.

sentences.en: Tim Stockwell, who headed the Canadian Institute for Substance Use Research from 2004 to 2020, said adding the stimulation of energy drinks to the impaired judgment caused by alcohol is a recipe for risky behavior.
sentences.zh: 2004 年至 2020 年间担任加拿大药物使用研究所所长的蒂姆·斯托克韦尔 (Tim Stockwell) 表示，在酒精导致的判断力受损的基础上加上能量饮料的刺激，会导致危险行为。

blocks.html_en: The caffeine in energy drinks ranges from 80 mg in a Red Bull, slightly less than a typical cup of coffee, to 300 mg in other brands. But energy drinks also contain ingredients such as taurine and guarana that can magnify its effects on the body.

sentences.en: The caffeine in energy drinks ranges from 80 mg in a Red Bull, slightly less than a typical cup of coffee, to 300 mg in other brands.
sentences.zh: 能量饮料中的咖啡因含量从红牛的 80 毫克（略低于一杯典型的咖啡）到其他品牌的 300 毫克不等。

sentences.en: But energy drinks also contain ingredients such as taurine and guarana that can magnify its effects on the body.
sentences.zh: 但能量饮料还含有牛磺酸和瓜拉那等成分，可以放大其对身体的影响。

blocks.html_en: “It's a pretty potentially dangerous combination, giving you the energy to do crazy, daft things,” Stockwell said, “and something that takes away the fear of the consequences.”

sentences.en: “It's a pretty potentially dangerous combination, giving you the energy to do crazy, daft things,” Stockwell said, “and something that takes away the fear of the consequences.”
sentences.zh: 斯托克韦尔说：“这是一个相当潜在危险的组合，它给你能量去做疯狂、愚蠢的事情，并且消除对后果的恐惧。”

blocks.html_en: People have been hurt or killed all over the world after consuming alcohol and energy drinks, according to news reports. In England, an 18-year-old woman suffered three cardiac arrests after downing 10 Jägerbombs, a cocktail that combines an energy drink with the spirit Jägermeister. In Washington state, a 17-year-old boy died of acute alcohol intoxication after mixing hard liquor and energy drinks while playing video games with friends. In Quebec, a 14-year-old girl was found dead behind her school after consuming a caffeinated alcoholic drink called FCKD UP.

sentences.en: People have been hurt or killed all over the world after consuming alcohol and energy drinks, according to news reports.
sentences.zh: 据新闻报道，世界各地都有人因饮用酒精和能量饮料而受伤或死亡。

sentences.en: In England, an 18-year-old woman suffered three cardiac arrests after downing 10 Jägerbombs, a cocktail that combines an energy drink with the spirit Jägermeister.
sentences.zh: 在英格兰，一名 18 岁的女性在喝下 10 杯 Jägerbombs（一种将能量饮料与 Jägermeister 烈酒混合在一起的鸡尾酒）后，导致 3 次心脏骤停。

sentences.en: In Washington state, a 17-year-old boy died of acute alcohol intoxication after mixing hard liquor and energy drinks while playing video games with friends.
sentences.zh: 在华盛顿州，一名 17 岁男孩在与朋友玩电子游戏时混合烈性酒和能量饮料后死于急性酒精中毒。

sentences.en: In Quebec, a 14-year-old girl was found dead behind her school after consuming a caffeinated alcoholic drink called FCKD UP.
sentences.zh: 在魁北克省，一名 14 岁女孩在饮用名为 FCKD UP 的含咖啡因酒精饮料后被发现死在学校后面。

blocks.html_en: A considerable body of research suggests that incidents like these aren’t just chance or circumstance. Mixing alcohol and energy drinks was linked to higher rates of binge drinking, sexual abuse and drunk driving, according to a study conducted among U.S. college students. Another study of hospital patients in Canada found the combination was tied to higher levels of injury; among women, the risk of injury tripled.

sentences.en: A considerable body of research suggests that incidents like these aren’t just chance or circumstance.
sentences.zh: 大量研究表明，此类事件不仅仅是偶然或环境因素。

sentences.en: Mixing alcohol and energy drinks was linked to higher rates of binge drinking, sexual abuse and drunk driving, according to a study conducted among U.S. college students.
sentences.zh: 一项针对美国大学生进行的研究显示，混合酒精和能量饮料与酗酒、性虐待和醉酒驾驶的发生率较高有关。

sentences.en: Another study of hospital patients in Canada found the combination was tied to higher levels of injury; among women, the risk of injury tripled.
sentences.zh: 另一项针对加拿大医院患者的研究发现，这种组合与更高程度的损伤有关。女性受伤的风险增加了两倍。

blocks.html_en: Health authorities have shared these views. The U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention warn that mixing alcohol and energy drinks can lead to more drinking and a greater risk of injury, drunk driving and unwanted or unprotected sex.

sentences.en: Health authorities have shared these views.
sentences.zh: 卫生当局也同意这些观点。

sentences.en: The U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention warn that mixing alcohol and energy drinks can lead to more drinking and a greater risk of injury, drunk driving and unwanted or unprotected sex.
sentences.zh: 美国疾病控制和预防中心警告说，混合酒精和能量饮料可能会导致饮酒量增加，受伤、醉酒驾驶以及不受欢迎或无保护性行为的风险更大。

blocks.html_en: This research was just emerging back in 2010 during a string of deaths involving young people and Four Loko. The FDA acted quickly, ordering Four Loko and other companies to stop selling caffeinated alcoholic drinks.

sentences.en: This research was just emerging back in 2010 during a string of deaths involving young people and Four Loko.
sentences.zh: 这项研究刚刚在 2010 年出现，当时发生了一系列涉及年轻人和四洛克的死亡事件。

sentences.en: The FDA acted quickly, ordering Four Loko and other companies to stop selling caffeinated alcoholic drinks.
sentences.zh: FDA 迅速采取行动，命令 Four Loko 和其他公司停止销售含咖啡因的酒精饮料。

blocks.html_en: At the time of Mitchell’s death, energy drinks in Canada carried a warning saying not to mix them with alcohol. The coroner investigating his death criticized those warnings, writing that they were “insufficient” and “in small print.”

sentences.en: At the time of Mitchell’s death, energy drinks in Canada carried a warning saying not to mix them with alcohol.
sentences.zh: 米切尔去世时，加拿大的能量饮料上有一条警告，称不要将其与酒精混合。

sentences.en: The coroner investigating his death criticized those warnings, writing that they were “insufficient” and “in small print.”
sentences.zh: 调查他死亡的验尸官批评了这些警告，并写道这些警告“不够充分”而且“都是小字”。

blocks.html_en: Heather Mitchell said that neither she nor her son were fully aware of the risks of energy drinks. She said she really didn’t know if he frequently drank them. She assumed that if they were on the shelf, they were safe.

sentences.en: Heather Mitchell said that neither she nor her son were fully aware of the risks of energy drinks.
sentences.zh: 希瑟·米切尔说，她和她的儿子都没有完全意识到能量饮料的风险。

sentences.en: She said she really didn’t know if he frequently drank them.
sentences.zh: 她说她真的不知道他是否经常喝。

sentences.en: She assumed that if they were on the shelf, they were safe.
sentences.zh: 她认为如果它们在架子上，那么它们就是安全的。

blocks.html_en: Red Bull gets into the research business

sentences.en: Red Bull gets into the research business
sentences.zh: 红牛涉足研究业务

sentences.en: Red Bull funded a series of studies, many co-authored by Verster at Utrecht University, that found that mixing alcohol and energy drinks did not increase drinking or harm.
sentences.zh: 红牛资助了一系列研究，其中许多研究是由乌得勒支大学的维斯特合着的，这些研究发现混合酒精和能量饮料不会增加饮酒量或造成伤害。

sentences.en: Other researchers questioned the studies’ validity.Illustration by The Examination/Evident Media
sentences.zh: 其他研究人员质疑这些研究的有效性。插图由 The Examination/Evident Media 提供

blocks.html_en: In 2011, soon after becoming director of an injury prevention research center at Boston University, Jonathan Howland joined two Red Bull executives for dinner. One of them was Niederreiter, who was in charge of science for the company. Lobster was on the menu and a scientific collaboration was taking shape.

sentences.en: In 2011, soon after becoming director of an injury prevention research center at Boston University, Jonathan Howland joined two Red Bull executives for dinner.
sentences.zh: 2011 年，乔纳森·霍兰 (Jonathan Howland) 成为波士顿大学伤害预防研究中心主任后不久，就与两位红牛高管共进晚餐。

sentences.en: One of them was Niederreiter, who was in charge of science for the company.
sentences.zh: Niederreiter 就是其中之一，他负责公司的科学工作。

sentences.en: Lobster was on the menu and a scientific collaboration was taking shape.
sentences.zh: 龙虾出现在菜单上，一项科学合作正在形成。

blocks.html_en: Howland, who believed the FDA had overstepped the evidence with its ban on caffeinated alcoholic beverages, had taken note of ongoing research by Verster, the Dutch professor. The two ran in similar academic circles; both were members of a small group of researchers who studied alcohol hangovers. Verster’s preliminary findings suggested that mixing alcohol and energy drinks did not cause people to drink more or suffer higher rates of harm.

sentences.en: Howland, who believed the FDA had overstepped the evidence with its ban on caffeinated alcoholic beverages, had taken note of ongoing research by Verster, the Dutch professor.
sentences.zh: 霍兰认为 FDA 对含咖啡因酒精饮料的禁令超越了证据，他注意到荷兰教授维斯特正在进行的研究。

sentences.en: The two ran in similar academic circles; both were members of a small group of researchers who studied alcohol hangovers.
sentences.zh: 两人的学术圈子相似；两人都是研究酒精宿醉的一小群研究人员的成员。

sentences.en: Verster’s preliminary findings suggested that mixing alcohol and energy drinks did not cause people to drink more or suffer higher rates of harm.
sentences.zh: 维斯特的初步研究结果表明，混合酒精和能量饮料不会导致人们饮酒更多或遭受更高的伤害。

blocks.html_en: When Verster said he wanted to replicate his study in the United States, Howland didn’t hesitate. “I just jumped on it,” he said in an interview. That led to a deal between Red Bull and Boston University.

sentences.en: When Verster said he wanted to replicate his study in the United States, Howland didn’t hesitate.
sentences.zh: 当维斯特说他想在美国复制他的研究时，豪兰毫不犹豫。

sentences.en: “I just jumped on it,” he said in an interview.
sentences.zh: “我只是跳了起来，”他在接受采访时说道。

sentences.en: That led to a deal between Red Bull and Boston University.
sentences.zh: 这促成了红牛和波士顿大学之间的交易。

blocks.html_en: The key to Verster’s research was that he didn’t look for differences between people who drank only alcohol and people who consumed both alcohol and energy drinks, Verster told The Examination. Instead, he built his studies around people who did both, comparing outcomes between when they consumed alcohol alone and when they consumed it with energy drinks.

sentences.en: The key to Verster’s research was that he didn’t look for differences between people who drank only alcohol and people who consumed both alcohol and energy drinks, Verster told The Examination.
sentences.zh: 维斯特告诉《The Examination》，维斯特研究的关键在于，他并没有寻找只喝酒的人和同时喝酒精和能量饮料的人之间的差异。

sentences.en: Instead, he built his studies around people who did both, comparing outcomes between when they consumed alcohol alone and when they consumed it with energy drinks.
sentences.zh: 相反，他的研究围绕同时饮酒的人进行，比较了他们单独饮酒和饮用能量饮料时的结果。

blocks.html_en: This eliminated variables such as personality type and enabled him to test for causality, Verster said.

sentences.en: This eliminated variables such as personality type and enabled him to test for causality, Verster said.
sentences.zh: 维斯特说，这消除了性格类型等变量，使他能够测试因果关系。

blocks.html_en: But several months after Howland and his team started the project, they discovered a problem in how the study was set up. The details of the dispute were laid out in emails, study documents, and interviews with Howland and Tamara Calise, who consulted with the Boston team as a research expert.

sentences.en: But several months after Howland and his team started the project, they discovered a problem in how the study was set up.
sentences.zh: 但在豪兰和他的团队启动该项目几个月后，他们发现了研究的建立方式存在问题。

sentences.en: The details of the dispute were laid out in emails, study documents, and interviews with Howland and Tamara Calise, who consulted with the Boston team as a research expert.
sentences.zh: 电子邮件、研究文件以及对 Howland 和 Tamara Calise 的采访中列出了争议的细节，他们作为研究专家向波士顿团队提供了咨询。

blocks.html_en: The Boston researchers were alarmed because the survey that Verster’s team had provided defined alcohol mixed with energy drinks to include only alcoholic beverages consumed within two hours of an energy drink. That could underestimate binge drinking and harm linked to energy drinks, Howland’s team determined. There was no restriction on which drinks were counted when participants drank alcohol alone.

sentences.en: The Boston researchers were alarmed because the survey that Verster’s team had provided defined alcohol mixed with energy drinks to include only alcoholic beverages consumed within two hours of an energy drink.
sentences.zh: 波士顿研究人员感到震惊，因为调查显示，维斯特团队提供了与能量饮料混合的特定酒精，仅包括在能量饮料两小时内饮用的酒精饮料。

sentences.en: That could underestimate binge drinking and harm linked to energy drinks, Howland’s team determined.
sentences.zh: 豪兰的团队确定，这可能低估了酗酒和与能量饮料相关的危害。

sentences.en: There was no restriction on which drinks were counted when participants drank alcohol alone.
sentences.zh: 当参与者单独饮酒时，对于计算哪些饮料没有限制。

blocks.html_en: Howland and his colleagues urged Verster to change his approach. Verster refused. Howland said the message was clear: that “if you want the money, you do it exactly the way we tell you.”

sentences.en: Howland and his colleagues urged Verster to change his approach.
sentences.zh: 霍兰和他的同事敦促维斯特改变他的做法。

sentences.en: Verster refused.
sentences.zh: 维斯特拒绝了。

sentences.en: Howland said the message was clear: that “if you want the money, you do it exactly the way we tell you.”
sentences.zh: 霍兰表示，传达的信息很明确：“如果你想要钱，就按照我们告诉你的方式去做。”

blocks.html_en: Howland's team ultimately decided to back out of the study.

sentences.en: Howland's team ultimately decided to back out of the study.
sentences.zh: 豪兰的团队最终决定退出这项研究。

blocks.html_en: “We decided that we cannot use our university positions and professional reputations to recruit for a study that we believe cannot test important hypotheses in an unbiased way,” Howland wrote to Verster in June 2012.

sentences.en: “We decided that we cannot use our university positions and professional reputations to recruit for a study that we believe cannot test important hypotheses in an unbiased way,” Howland wrote to Verster in June 2012.
sentences.zh: “我们决定不能利用我们的大学职位和专业声誉来招募我们认为无法以公正的方式检验重要假设的研究，”Howland 在 2012 年 6 月写给 Verster 的信中说道。

sentences.en: Jonathan Howland (left), and Verster (third from right) were both members of a group of academics who studied alcohol hangovers.
sentences.zh: 乔纳森·豪兰（左）和维斯特（右三）都是研究酒精宿醉的学者小组的成员。

sentences.en: Here, members of that group and their guests, including Howland’s wife Elizabeth (right) eat lobster in Nova Scotia as part of a meeting in 2012.Photo provided to The Examination
sentences.zh: 图中，作为 2012 年会议的一部分，该团体的成员和他们的客人，包括 Howland 的妻子 Elizabeth（右）在新斯科舍省吃龙虾。照片提供给 The Examination

blocks.html_en: That didn’t seem to affect Red Bull’s support of Verster’s research. Later that year, he and four colleagues published a study of Dutch students, funded by the company, that used the disputed approach and came to a surprising conclusion: People were better off when they mixed alcohol with energy drinks than when they drank alcohol alone. When they combined the two, they drank less alcohol and were less likely to suffer harmful consequences, the study concluded.

sentences.en: That didn’t seem to affect Red Bull’s support of Verster’s research.
sentences.zh: 这似乎并没有影响红牛对维斯特研究的支持。

sentences.en: Later that year, he and four colleagues published a study of Dutch students, funded by the company, that used the disputed approach and came to a surprising conclusion: People were better off when they mixed alcohol with energy drinks than when they drank alcohol alone.
sentences.zh: 同年晚些时候，他和四位同事发表了一项由该公司资助的荷兰学生研究，该研究使用了有争议的方法，并得出了一个令人惊讶的结论：人们将酒精与能量饮料混合时比单独饮用酒精时效果更好。

sentences.en: When they combined the two, they drank less alcohol and were less likely to suffer harmful consequences, the study concluded.
sentences.zh: 研究得出结论，当他们将两者结合起来时，他们的饮酒量会减少，并且不太可能遭受有害后果。

blocks.html_en: Five alcohol researchers consulted by The Examination said they agreed with the Boston researchers that the approach by Verster’s team was flawed. The half-life of caffeine is five to six hours — meaning that five to six hours after someone ingests caffeine, half of it remains in their system and continues to affect them. That’s significantly longer than the time window used by Verster.

sentences.en: Five alcohol researchers consulted by The Examination said they agreed with the Boston researchers that the approach by Verster’s team was flawed.
sentences.zh: 《The Examination》咨询的五名酒精研究人员表示，他们同意波士顿研究人员的观点，即维斯特团队的方法存在缺陷。

sentences.en: The half-life of caffeine is five to six hours — meaning that five to six hours after someone ingests caffeine, half of it remains in their system and continues to affect them.
sentences.zh: 咖啡因的半衰期为五到六个小时，这意味着在摄入咖啡因五到六个小时后，一半的咖啡因会留在他们的系统中并继续影响他们。

sentences.en: That’s significantly longer than the time window used by Verster.
sentences.zh: 这比 Verster 使用的时间窗口要长得多。

blocks.html_en: From 2016 to 2021, Verster and other Red Bull-funded scientists in the U.K. and Australia published at least five more studies that used the same definition of mixing alcohol and energy drinks. All concluded that mixing did not lead to increased drinking or harm.

sentences.en: From 2016 to 2021, Verster and other Red Bull-funded scientists in the U.K. and Australia published at least five more studies that used the same definition of mixing alcohol and energy drinks.
sentences.zh: 从 2016 年到 2021 年，维斯特和英国和澳大利亚的其他红牛资助的科学家至少发表了五项研究，这些研究使用了混合酒精和能量饮料的相同定义。

sentences.en: All concluded that mixing did not lead to increased drinking or harm.
sentences.zh: 所有人的结论是，混合不会导致饮酒量增加或造成伤害。

blocks.html_en: Laura Schmidt, a professor at the University of California, San Francisco who has examined research funded by the food and beverage industry, described those studies as “marketing dressed up as science.”

sentences.en: Laura Schmidt, a professor at the University of California, San Francisco who has examined research funded by the food and beverage industry, described those studies as “marketing dressed up as science.”
sentences.zh: 加州大学旧金山分校教授劳拉·施密特（Laura Schmidt）研究了食品和饮料行业资助的研究，她将这些研究描述为“披着科学外衣的营销”。

blocks.html_en: William Kerr, scientific director at the federally funded National Alcohol Research Center, said, “Aspects of the studies seem biased to deliver counterintuitive results that support industry perspectives.”

sentences.en: William Kerr, scientific director at the federally funded National Alcohol Research Center, said, “Aspects of the studies seem biased to deliver counterintuitive results that support industry perspectives.”
sentences.zh: 联邦政府资助的国家酒精研究中心的科学主任威廉·克尔（William Kerr）表示：“这些研究的某些方面似乎有偏见，提供了支持行业观点的违反直觉的结果。”

blocks.html_en: We decided that we cannot use our university positions and professional reputations to recruit for a study that we believe cannot test important hypotheses in an unbiased way.

sentences.en: We decided that we cannot use our university positions and professional reputations to recruit for a study that we believe cannot test important hypotheses in an unbiased way.
sentences.zh: 我们决定不能利用我们的大学职位和专业声誉来招募我们认为无法以公正的方式检验重要假设的研究。

blocks.html_en: Jonathan Howland, in an email to Joris Verster in June 2012

sentences.en: Jonathan Howland, in an email to Joris Verster in June 2012
sentences.zh: Jonathan Howland，2012 年 6 月给 Joris Verster 的电子邮件

blocks.html_en: In an email to The Examination, Verster acknowledged that the Boston researchers raised questions about the study methodology. He said he didn’t change it because he wanted the study to be comparable to his earlier research.

sentences.en: In an email to The Examination, Verster acknowledged that the Boston researchers raised questions about the study methodology.
sentences.zh: 在给 The Examination 的一封电子邮件中，维斯特承认波士顿研究人员对研究方法提出了疑问。

sentences.en: He said he didn’t change it because he wanted the study to be comparable to his earlier research.
sentences.zh: 他说他没有改变它，因为他希望这项研究与他早期的研究具有可比性。

content_html_zh:
这篇报道由 STAT 联合发表，是“Behind the Buzz”项目的一部分，该项目是一项调查合作项目，涉及 The Examination、The Bristol Cable、Daraj、Investico、Paper Trail Media、Der Spiegel、Der Standard 和 Toronto Star。

一个冬天的早晨，在距纽约市摩天大楼以东约两小时车程的长岛小镇，一位荷兰研究人员告诉当地官员，他们对将大量咖啡因的能量饮料与酒精混合的担忧被夸大了。

几个月前，美国食品和药物管理局实际上禁止了 Four Loko，这是一种被大学生称为“罐头停电”的含咖啡因麦芽酒。 萨福克县郊区现在正在考虑采取更全面的措施：禁止向未成年人出售能量饮料。

乌得勒支大学学者乔里斯·维斯特表示，这项法律没有科学依据。 尽管酒和能量饮料经常一起饮用，但维斯特认为，红牛等饮料并不是人们喝醉时发生的坏事的罪魁祸首。

他提出了一个可能会引起当地人共鸣的类比；萨福克县的海滩小镇是惊悚片《大白鲨》的灵感来源。 他说，将酗酒和酒精引起的伤害归咎于能量饮料，就像将鲨鱼袭击归咎于夏季冰淇淋的销售一样。

“鲨鱼袭击事件并不是冰淇淋销售造成的，”维斯特在 2011 年 2 月的听证会上表示。

他是跨越大西洋敦促官员放弃该提案的三名科学家之一。 其他人是一位英国教授和红牛的首席科学官。 这三人的共同点不仅仅是研究兴趣：通过薪水或研究资助，三人都从世界上最大的能量饮料公司红牛那里获得了资金。

他们的论点赢得了胜利。 立法者取消了年龄限制，标志着这家总部位于奥地利的公司在一场利用科学来对抗对其产品的限制的全球运动中取得了早期胜利。

一项由 The Examination、The Bristol Cable、Daraj、Investico、Paper Trail Media、Der Spiegel、Der Standard、STAT 和 Toronto Star 联合调查发现，十多年来，红牛为大学教授支付了数十万美元进行对能量饮料行业有利的研究。 该公司已将学者送往美国城市，并为与正在考虑限制能量饮料的政府官员的会议提供谈话要点。 它为英国的一名研究人员和荷兰的另一名研究人员提供了博士学位。

在美国和加拿大，由红牛支持或由与该公司有财务关系的学者进行的研究已被用来击败年龄限制和警告标签等措施。

欧洲一家食品机构 2015 年的一份重要报告引用了这些研究，发现没有明确的证据表明混合能量饮料和酒精有害。 该报告仍然是欧洲的最终决定，并已被用来阻止其他地方采取行动。

红牛支持的研究几乎一致地传达了这样的信息：同时饮用能量饮料和酒精并不比单独饮酒更有害。

这与该主题的绝大多数独立研究形成鲜明对比。

该检查收集了 100 多项有关能量饮料和酒精混合的健康或行为风险的研究。 在获得红牛资助或由披露与该公司存在财务利益冲突的研究人员进行的研究中，95% 的结论是，将酒精与能量饮料混合不会增加这些风险。 The Examination 发现，大约 80% 的独立研究得出了相反的结论。

公司经常资助有争议产品的研究，这种做法受到健康倡导者的批评。 但主要的酒精研究人员在审查了一些与红牛有经济关系的研究后表示，还有更深层次的问题。

他们说，许多研究存在缺陷，这引发了人们对其结论的质疑。 在波士顿，荷兰研究人员维斯特拒绝解决他们认为会使结果产生偏差的问题后，一组科学家退出了红牛资助的一项研究。

红牛全球科学、监管和政府事务主管 Karlheinz Niederreiter 在给 The Examination 及其合作伙伴的一份简短声明中写道：“世界各地的卫生当局已得出结论，红牛能量饮料可以安全饮用。” 他写道，这就是为什么去年全球销售了近 140 亿罐。

尼德雷特和其他红牛高管没有回答有关新闻媒体调查结果的问题，包括有关与酒精一起饮用能量饮料的安全性的问题。

美国和欧洲行业组织发布的自愿指南称，红牛和怪兽饮料公司等成员公司不提倡将能量饮料与酒精混合，也不声称能量饮料可以抵消酒精的作用。 该欧洲组织表示，学术研究发现，将两者混合不会带来额外的风险。

澳大利亚迪肯大学教授彼得·米勒表示，新闻媒体的调查结果并不令人意外。 早在 2013 年，也就是大部分研究发表的时候，他在一本医学杂志上写了一篇文章，批评行业资助的有关混合能量饮料和酒精的研究浪潮。

米勒告诉《The Examination》，这些研究资助是“一项利用大学声誉来影响政策的投资”。 “这是一场保护他们的利润并避免立法干预的运动。”

他说，这很有效。 米勒说，红牛资助的研究人员“完全破坏了证据基础”。 “如果政客们不采取行动，就会引发这种怀疑。”

这项研究大部分是在公众对能量饮料安全性争论日益激烈的时期进行的。 特别是对于年轻人来说。 尤其是与酒精混合时。

醉得彻底清醒

2016 年 8 月的一个周末晚上，扎卡里·米切尔 (Zachary Mitchell) 与一些朋友一起在魁北克省的一处湖边小屋度假。 他的母亲说，这位 21 岁的男孩几乎每个夏季周末都会去这间小屋。

根据验尸官的报告，米切尔在大约两个小时内喝了几罐红牛和大约六瓶啤酒，然后他和他的朋友决定去游泳。

米切尔出生在湖边，从小就学会游泳。 “他是一条鱼，”他的母亲希瑟·米切尔说。

但在午夜前不久，米切尔从 15 英尺高的甲板上跳水，笨拙地落入水中。 他短暂地浮出水面，说了几句话，然后又沉下去了。 根据验尸官的报告，这是他的朋友们最后一次见到他。

验尸官写道，米切尔溺水身亡，很可能是由于能量饮料和体育锻炼相结合引发的心律失常所致。 她指出，他的血液酒精含量约为 0.1%，略高于驾驶的法定上限。

她在报告中呼吁“针对年轻受众开展大规模的广告宣传活动”，宣传能量饮料的风险，包括将其与酒精混合的风险。

研究人员有一个术语来表达他们对混合酒精和能量饮料的担忧：完全清醒的醉酒。

2004 年至 2020 年间担任加拿大药物使用研究所所长的蒂姆·斯托克韦尔 (Tim Stockwell) 表示，在酒精导致的判断力受损的基础上加上能量饮料的刺激，会导致危险行为。

能量饮料中的咖啡因含量从红牛的 80 毫克（略低于一杯典型的咖啡）到其他品牌的 300 毫克不等。 但能量饮料还含有牛磺酸和瓜拉那等成分，可以放大其对身体的影响。

斯托克韦尔说：“这是一个相当潜在危险的组合，它给你能量去做疯狂、愚蠢的事情，并且消除对后果的恐惧。”

据新闻报道，世界各地都有人因饮用酒精和能量饮料而受伤或死亡。 在英格兰，一名 18 岁的女性在喝下 10 杯 Jägerbombs（一种将能量饮料与 Jägermeister 烈酒混合在一起的鸡尾酒）后，导致 3 次心脏骤停。 在华盛顿州，一名 17 岁男孩在与朋友玩电子游戏时混合烈性酒和能量饮料后死于急性酒精中毒。 在魁北克省，一名 14 岁女孩在饮用名为 FCKD UP 的含咖啡因酒精饮料后被发现死在学校后面。

大量研究表明，此类事件不仅仅是偶然或环境因素。 一项针对美国大学生进行的研究显示，混合酒精和能量饮料与酗酒、性虐待和醉酒驾驶的发生率较高有关。 另一项针对加拿大医院患者的研究发现，这种组合与更高程度的损伤有关。女性受伤的风险增加了两倍。

卫生当局也同意这些观点。 美国疾病控制和预防中心警告说，混合酒精和能量饮料可能会导致饮酒量增加，受伤、醉酒驾驶以及不受欢迎或无保护性行为的风险更大。

这项研究刚刚在 2010 年出现，当时发生了一系列涉及年轻人和四洛克的死亡事件。 FDA 迅速采取行动，命令 Four Loko 和其他公司停止销售含咖啡因的酒精饮料。

米切尔去世时，加拿大的能量饮料上有一条警告，称不要将其与酒精混合。 调查他死亡的验尸官批评了这些警告，并写道这些警告“不够充分”而且“都是小字”。

希瑟·米切尔说，她和她的儿子都没有完全意识到能量饮料的风险。 她说她真的不知道他是否经常喝。 她认为如果它们在架子上，那么它们就是安全的。

红牛涉足研究业务

2011 年，乔纳森·霍兰 (Jonathan Howland) 成为波士顿大学伤害预防研究中心主任后不久，就与两位红牛高管共进晚餐。 Niederreiter 就是其中之一，他负责公司的科学工作。 龙虾出现在菜单上，一项科学合作正在形成。

霍兰认为 FDA 对含咖啡因酒精饮料的禁令超越了证据，他注意到荷兰教授维斯特正在进行的研究。 两人的学术圈子相似；两人都是研究酒精宿醉的一小群研究人员的成员。 维斯特的初步研究结果表明，混合酒精和能量饮料不会导致人们饮酒更多或遭受更高的伤害。

当维斯特说他想在美国复制他的研究时，豪兰毫不犹豫。 “我只是跳了起来，”他在接受采访时说道。 这促成了红牛和波士顿大学之间的交易。

维斯特告诉《The Examination》，维斯特研究的关键在于，他并没有寻找只喝酒的人和同时喝酒精和能量饮料的人之间的差异。 相反，他的研究围绕同时饮酒的人进行，比较了他们单独饮酒和饮用能量饮料时的结果。

维斯特说，这消除了性格类型等变量，使他能够测试因果关系。

但在豪兰和他的团队启动该项目几个月后，他们发现了研究的建立方式存在问题。 电子邮件、研究文件以及对 Howland 和 Tamara Calise 的采访中列出了争议的细节，他们作为研究专家向波士顿团队提供了咨询。

波士顿研究人员感到震惊，因为调查显示，维斯特团队提供了与能量饮料混合的特定酒精，仅包括在能量饮料两小时内饮用的酒精饮料。 豪兰的团队确定，这可能低估了酗酒和与能量饮料相关的危害。 当参与者单独饮酒时，对于计算哪些饮料没有限制。

霍兰和他的同事敦促维斯特改变他的做法。 维斯特拒绝了。 霍兰表示，传达的信息很明确：“如果你想要钱，就按照我们告诉你的方式去做。”

豪兰的团队最终决定退出这项研究。

“我们决定不能利用我们的大学职位和专业声誉来招募我们认为无法以公正的方式检验重要假设的研究，”Howland 在 2012 年 6 月写给 Verster 的信中说道。

这似乎并没有影响红牛对维斯特研究的支持。 同年晚些时候，他和四位同事发表了一项由该公司资助的荷兰学生研究，该研究使用了有争议的方法，并得出了一个令人惊讶的结论：人们将酒精与能量饮料混合时比单独饮用酒精时效果更好。 研究得出结论，当他们将两者结合起来时，他们的饮酒量会减少，并且不太可能遭受有害后果。

《The Examination》咨询的五名酒精研究人员表示，他们同意波士顿研究人员的观点，即维斯特团队的方法存在缺陷。 咖啡因的半衰期为五到六个小时，这意味着在摄入咖啡因五到六个小时后，一半的咖啡因会留在他们的系统中并继续影响他们。 这比 Verster 使用的时间窗口要长得多。

从 2016 年到 2021 年，维斯特和英国和澳大利亚的其他红牛资助的科学家至少发表了五项研究，这些研究使用了混合酒精和能量饮料的相同定义。 所有人的结论是，混合不会导致饮酒量增加或造成伤害。

加州大学旧金山分校教授劳拉·施密特（Laura Schmidt）研究了食品和饮料行业资助的研究，她将这些研究描述为“披着科学外衣的营销”。

联邦政府资助的国家酒精研究中心的科学主任威廉·克尔（William Kerr）表示：“这些研究的某些方面似乎有偏见，提供了支持行业观点的违反直觉的结果。”

我们决定不能利用我们的大学职位和专业声誉来招募我们认为无法以公正的方式检验重要假设的研究。

Jonathan Howland，2012 年 6 月给 Joris Verster 的电子邮件

在给 The Examination 的一封电子邮件中，维斯特承认波士顿研究人员对研究方法提出了疑问。 他说他没有改变它，因为他希望这项研究与他早期的研究具有可比性。

关于酒精饮料和能量饮料混合的定义，他写道，两小时的限制是为了排除当天早些时候饮用的能量饮料，而不是限制酒精饮料的数量。

乌得勒支大学十多年前就调查了维斯特与红牛合作中潜在的利益冲突。 该大学认为，维斯特的透明度不够，因为他通过自己的公司获得报酬，进行研究，而这些研究引用了他的大学隶属关系。 然而，该大学得出的结论是，这并不违反诚信。

在荷兰新闻媒体 Investico 最近对维斯特的研究进行询问后，该大学表示，维斯特违反了其管理外部资助研究的政策。 该大学表示，它不知道这项工作的范围，而且维斯特在引用其大学隶属关系的同时继续接受私人报酬是一个问题。

该大学表示，这些调查“引发了内部问题”，并且正在成立一个委员会来调查维斯特研究小组内的“科学文化和科学质量政策”。

维斯特是红牛支持的研究人员中最多产的，他否认自己违反了道德准则，并表示他坚持自己的研究。 他将对他的工作的批评归因于科学分歧。

英国布里斯托尔电报发现，肖恩·约翰逊（Sean Johnson）的博士学位由红牛资助，他与维斯特一起发表了几项研究，他对红牛资助的研究的进行方式表示保留。

约翰逊在 2023 年提交的评论中反思了他的早期研究，这是他博士论文的一部分。 他写道，关于混合酒精和能量饮料的研究似乎已经变得政治化；有时，经历同行评审过程“感觉就像身处战壕中”。 后来，他对那段时期的看法发生了转变。

“我可能对我的学术团体和行业资助者的立场产生了无意识的偏见，”约翰逊写道。 在“资助者”后面的括号中，他写道：“红牛有限公司”。

约翰逊没有回应多次的置评请求。

“科学就是科学，无论谁资助它”

与红牛有经济联系的关于酒精和能量饮料风险的研究数量相对较少，但这些研究仍然具有影响力。 英国、加拿大、澳大利亚、西班牙和爱尔兰的政府或咨询机构关于能量饮料政策的报告引用了这些研究。

最重要的是欧洲食品安全局的一份报告。 作为欧盟食品问题的科学顾问，其观点不仅为欧洲政策提供参考，而且在国际上也具有影响力。

2015年，该机构发布了一份全面的报告，广泛认可咖啡因和能量饮料的安全性。 关于能量饮料和酒精的组合的三个部分引用了维斯特的研究。

最详细的讨论来自 Verster 和三位之前接受过红牛资助的同事 2014 年撰写的一项研究。 他们回顾了实验室研究，以确定酒精和咖啡因混合是否会导致人们在没有意识到的情况下喝醉，这种现象被称为“掩蔽”。 他们的结论是，蒙面并不是威胁。

几位酒精研究人员告诉《The Examination》，虽然掩蔽当时是一个研究课题，但对于能量饮料和酒精来说，这并不是最严重的问题。 他们说，更重要的是，能量饮料可以促使人们喝更多的酒，而两者的结合会产生一种兴奋和去抑制的感觉——“完全清醒的醉酒”。

欧洲食品管理局的报告呼应了维斯特及其同事的结论，即掩盖——更一般地说，混合酒精和能量饮料——并不是一个严重的问题。 食品管理局的报告没有指出这些研究披露了研究人员与红牛的关系。

欧洲食品安全局科学家 Silvia Valtueña Martínez 为其 2015 年报告做出了贡献，并为其研究结果进行了辩护。 她说，作者考虑了广泛的研究，并且像红牛这样的行业支持的研究不应被忽视。

“科学就是科学，无论谁资助它，”她说。

尽管食品管理局最近表示将重新审视其关于咖啡因和能量饮料的调查结果，但《今日马耳他》报道称，它不打算解决混合能量饮料和酒精的风险。

十多年来，食品管理局的报告一直是欧洲及其他地区能量饮料的重要参考；英国、加拿大、德国等国家的政府和咨询机构均引用了它。

饮料行业也是如此，用它来反对能量饮料的法规。

科学就是科学，不管谁资助它。

Silvia Valtueña Martínez，欧洲食品安全局科学家

其中一项努力是在米切尔去世几年后在加拿大进行的。

他去世时能量饮料罐上的酒精警告标签是临时措施的结果。 2021 年，加拿大公共卫生机构加拿大卫生部提议将这一警告永久化，并指出将酒精与能量饮料混合已“被确定为公共卫生问题”。

饮料行业表示，该警告标签没有科学依据，并且有研究支持其立场。

加拿大饮料协会向加拿大卫生部发送了一封信函，援引了三项研究。 他们所有人的作者都获得了红牛的资助。 欧盟也加入进来，对标签要求提出警告，并指出了欧洲食品安全局的报告。

一年后，加拿大卫生部态度大转变，不仅放弃了永久使用警告标签的提议，而且完全放弃了它。

加拿大卫生部在一份书面声明中告诉《The Examination》和《多伦多星报》，它“严重依赖”2015 年欧洲食品管理局的报告以及其自身的风险评估来做出这一决定。 该机构表示，它考虑了“广泛的信息”，包括已发表的研究和利益相关者提交的意见。

希瑟·米切尔称加拿大卫生部的决定“明显失职”。

在她失去儿子近十年后，加拿大的能量饮料罐提供的有关酒精风险的信息比儿子去世当晚还少。

哥伦比亚大学托尔数字新闻中心的计算记者艾斯瓦里亚·钱德拉塞卡 (Aisvarya Chandrasekar) 为数据分析做出了贡献。
